title: Module geometric stalks compute and detect unbounded cohomology
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $T$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] with the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and its module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ [def-weil-geometric-point], the stalk functor $s_{\bar t}:\operatorname{Mod}(A_T)\to\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], with the induced $A$-action, is exact. Forgetting module structures commutes with kernels, images, quotients and cohomology. Termwise $s_{\bar t}$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and induces a functor on the unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], denoted $E\mapsto E_{\bar t}$. For every $E\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $i\in\mathbf Z$ there is a natural $A$-linear isomorphism
$$ (\mathcal H^i(E))_{\bar t}\cong H^i(E_{\bar t}), $$
with cohomology sheaves as in [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Moreover
$$ \mathcal H^i(E)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad H^i(E_{\bar t})=0\text{ for every geometric point }\bar t. $$
No boundedness, finiteness, constructibility or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03PT (lemma-stalk-exact), clause (3), and Tag 03PU (theorem-exactness-stalks), applied to underlying abelian sheaves of constant-coefficient modules; the cohomology comparison used in sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0DJJ (lemma-tor-amplitude-stalk), converse proof

proof.text: Write $U:\operatorname{Mod}(A_T)\to\operatorname{Ab}(T_{\mathrm{et}})$ for the forgetful functor. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](1) to $\mathcal O=A_T$ on the small etale site: $U$ is faithful and exact and preserves kernels and cokernels. Apply [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology](a)-(c) to $U$. Since an image is the kernel of the cokernel and a quotient is a cokernel, forgetting scalars also preserves images, quotients and cohomology, naturally in a complex. For ordinary $A$-modules the same identifications are literal: the kernel and image are the same additive subgroups with the restricted action, and a quotient has the same additive cosets with $a[m]=[am]$. In particular an exact sequence of $A$-modules can be checked after forgetting to abelian groups.

For a geometric point $\bar t$, use the pointed-neighbourhood colimit of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. If $a\in A$ and $m\in\mathcal F(V)$, define $a[m]=[a_Vm]$, where $a_V\in A_T(V)$ is the constant section coming from sheafification of the constant presheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Restriction compatibility in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] gives $(a_Vm)|_W=a_W(m|_W)$, so this rule respects the colimit relations. The module identities hold on representatives and hence on germs. For a module-sheaf morphism $f$, $s_{\bar t}(f)(a[m])=[f(a_Vm)]=a[f(m)]$, so the stalk maps are $A$-linear. Addition of maps is also preserved on representatives. Forgetting this action gives exactly the stalk of $U\mathcal F$, since both use the same germs and relations.

source.place: Construction immediately before Tag 04EQ (lemma-stalk-exact-modules); etale-cohomology.tex Definition 040R (definition-stalk)

proof.text: Given a short exact sequence of $A_T$-module sheaves, step 1 makes its underlying abelian-sheaf sequence short exact. The abelian geometric stalk functor is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact]. Its resulting exact sequence of abelian groups is the underlying sequence of the $A$-linear stalk maps from step 2. The elementary kernel/image description for ordinary modules in step 1 therefore makes that sequence short exact in $\operatorname{Mod}(A)$. Thus $s_{\bar t}$ is additive and exact; no finiteness property of the ring, the scheme or the sheaves entered the argument.

Let $C$ be any integer-indexed cochain complex of $A_T$-modules, with no boundedness assumption. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] with $F=s_{\bar t}$, now an exact functor between abelian categories. In degree $i$, its comparison identifies the kernel of $s_{\bar t}(d^i)$ with $s_{\bar t}(\ker d^i)$ and the image of $s_{\bar t}(d^{i-1})$ with $s_{\bar t}(\operatorname{im}d^{i-1})$, compatibly with cycles and quotient projections. Taking the inverse of its natural comparison gives
$$s_{\bar t}(H^i(C))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(s_{\bar t}C).$$
It is an isomorphism in $\operatorname{Mod}(A)$, hence $A$-linear. This computation involves only the three consecutive terms in degrees $i-1,i,i+1$. If $f:C\to C'$ is a quasi-isomorphism, naturality identifies $H^i(s_{\bar t}f)$ with $s_{\bar t}(H^i(f))$, which is invertible for every $i$. Thus the termwise stalk functor preserves quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor), applied to consecutive terms; derived.tex Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to $s_{\bar t}$. It supplies a functor $D(s_{\bar t})$ on the full unbounded derived categories and a natural identification $D(s_{\bar t})(QC)\cong Q(s_{\bar t}C)$. Define $E_{\bar t}=D(s_{\bar t})(E)$. The representative description in [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] identifies $\mathcal H^i(QC)$ with $H^i(C)$. Consequently step 4 gives the required comparison $(\mathcal H^i(E))_{\bar t}\cong H^i(E_{\bar t})$. This is natural on the derived category: both cohomology functors invert quasi-isomorphisms, and the naturality equation of step 4 for a quasi-isomorphism remains valid for its inverse, by composing with the two inverse maps. Morphisms in the localization are generated by complex maps and these inverses [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so the same equation holds for every derived morphism. The comparison remains $A$-linear throughout.

Fix $i$ and put $\mathcal F=\mathcal H^i(E)$. If $\mathcal F=0$, its stalks are zero and the comparison just constructed gives $H^i(E_{\bar t})=0$ for every geometric point. Conversely, suppose these cohomology modules vanish. The comparison and step 2 show that every geometric stalk of the underlying abelian sheaf $U\mathcal F$ vanishes. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to $0\to U\mathcal F$: every stalk map is an isomorphism, so $0\to U\mathcal F$ is an isomorphism. Hence $U\mathcal F=0$. The faithfulness of $U$ in [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](1) now gives $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F}=0$, so $\mathcal F$ is a zero object. This proves the equivalence for each integer $i$. On the empty scheme the stalk condition is vacuous and the same conservativity assertion still applies. No truncation or convergence argument has been used.
